Attribution.description:
Where ``Utterance.speaker`` came from, and how much to trust it.

A wrong speaker is invisible — it sounds like a perfectly good take in the
wrong voice — while an ``Unknown`` is a work item somebody can see. So the
attributor records *why* it decided, and abstains (speaker ``"Unknown"``)
when the basis is weak: see ``attribute.ABSTAIN_BELOW``.

``basis``:
  - ``tag``          an explicit ``"…" said X`` / ``X said, "…"`` / ``X: "…"``
  - ``pronoun``      ``"…" she said`` resolved against the recent antecedent
  - ``continuation`` the same speaker continuing inside one paragraph
  - ``alternation``  back-and-forth across paragraphs (a guess, below the bar)
  - ``manual``       a person reassigned the line (studio ``PATCH /lines/{id}``)
  - ``none``         narration, or nothing to go on at all
Attribution.title: Attribution

AudioSpan.description: Filled after rendering. Powers the player timeline + incremental re-render.
AudioSpan.title: AudioSpan

CastPatchEntry.description:
One row of ``PATCH /cast``. Absent fields are left alone.

``create`` exists because a name the book
does not have is a typo far more often than it is a new character, so it is
a 404 unless the caller says it meant it.
CastPatchEntry.title: CastPatchEntry

DirectableCounts.description:
Lines routed to an engine that declares ``instruction`` — what a director
pass can actually stamp. ``POST /direct`` is a 409 when ``lines`` is 0.
DirectableCounts.title: DirectableCounts

ErrorDetail.description:
Every error the studio answers with, 4xx or 5xx: one human-readable line.

``app.py`` flattens FastAPI's 422 list and wraps unhandled exceptions into
this same shape, so it is the only error body a client ever has to parse.
ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail

Intent.description:
Engine-agnostic reading intent. An analyzer fills this in; Kokoro can't
consume it directly, so the renderer maps it onto voice/speed/pauses.
Intent.title: Intent

LinePatch.description:
``PATCH /books/{slug}/lines/{id}``.

Every field is optional and ``None`` means "clear"; "absent" and "null" are
told apart by ``model_fields_set``, never by a falsy check — clearing an
instruction and not mentioning it are different requests. Range/type checks
live here so a bad value is a 422 *before* anything touches the script;
cross-field checks (engine ↔ voice, spoken_text ↔ text ↔ tags) need the
line and the engine catalog, so they live in ``validate.py``.
LinePatch.title: LinePatch

LinePatchResult.description:
``PATCH /books/{slug}/lines/{id}``: the line as it now stands, and the
script version that edit left (unchanged by a QC-only mark).
LinePatchResult.title: LinePatchResult

LineRenderResult.description:
``POST /books/{slug}/lines/{id}/render``: the freshly cached line and the
URL its take plays from.
LineRenderResult.title: LineRenderResult

NeedsRenderCounts.description:
The two different reasons a book still owes you a render: lines whose
audio is not cached, and chapters whose WAV does not reflect their lines.
A single-line re-render empties the first and leaves the second — which is
the dead end the UI could not label before (Amendments v1.1).
NeedsRenderCounts.title: NeedsRenderCounts

PassScene.title: PassScene

QcCounts.description: Chapter sign-off tallies over the chapters that are in the audio.

VoiceOption.description:

delete.description:
Cancel first, then delete, then forget the jobs.

Deleting a book with a job in flight used to be a race the client never
heard about: 204, folder gone, and a few seconds later the dying job's
failure handler re-created ``output/<slug>/jobs/`` — an orphan folder no
endpoint would ever mention again. Cancellation is
cooperative, so this waits for the worker to acknowledge, bounded; the
job records go with the book rather than lingering as ghosts in
``GET /jobs``.

patch.description:
Edit one line. Absent key = leave alone, ``null`` = clear.

Two rules from the contract that are easy to get backwards:
editing ``text`` clears ``spoken_text`` (the tags were annotations of
the *old* words, so keeping them would send the engine a sentence the
reader never sees), and touching ``instruction``/``spoken_text`` stamps
``direction_source: "manual"`` so a later director pass leaves it alone;
clearing both puts the line back to ``"none"``.

Everything is validated **before** anything is assigned. The old handler
mutated the model field by field and saved: pydantic does not re-validate
on attribute assignment, so ``{"speed": 99}`` was written out and then
rejected on the next *load* — every later read of that book a 500, with
no way back through the API. Here the merged render
block is re-validated by ``schema.Render`` itself, the engine and voice
are checked against the catalog, and ``spoken_text`` has to be this
line's text plus tags the engine actually understands.

requestBody.description: Any subset of the fields; an absent key is left alone, null clears.

post.description:
Commit the decided scenes. Idempotent, and manual lines are safe.

``instruction_engines`` is the set of engines the *gateway* says accept a
written note, so a hybrid book stamps only the lines that can hear one;
with no gateway it falls back to the pass's own target engine rather
than stamping every line in the book.
